/-!
# Effective Computability of the Erdős-style Zero-Sum Threshold

This file studies the *effective computability* of the threshold in zero-sum
problems of Erdős–Ginzburg–Ziv (EGZ) type.  The research mission asks whether the
threshold `n₀(m₁, …, mₖ)` appearing in such theorems can be bounded above by an
explicitly computable function of the form `C · (m₁⋯mₖ)^poly(k, m₁, …, mₖ)`.

Our anchor result is the **Davenport-constant upper bound**
`D(G) ≤ |G|` for a finite abelian group `G`: every sequence of `|G|` elements of
`G` contains a nonempty zero-sum subsequence.  For the group
`G = ⊕ᵢ ZMod mᵢ` we have `|G| = ∏ᵢ mᵢ`, so the threshold is *exactly* of the
conjectured product form with absolute constant `C = 1` and polynomial exponent
`1`.  This makes the threshold effectively computable.

The proof is the classical prefix-sum pigeonhole argument and is genuinely
constructive: it exhibits a *consecutive* zero-sum subsequence.

This complements the Mathlib catalog theorem `ZMod.erdos_ginzburg_ziv`
(`Mathlib/Combinatorics/Additive/ErdosGinzburgZiv.lean`), which requires the
zero-sum subsequence to have a *prescribed* length `n` out of `2n-1` terms.

-- !-- Lab Notes -- !--
Hypothesis (Hypothesizer): For the additive group `G = ⊕ᵢ ZMod mᵢ`, the zero-sum
  threshold is bounded by `∏ᵢ mᵢ`, an explicit product-form (hence effectively
  computable) bound `C·(∏mᵢ)^poly` with `C = poly = 1`.
Experiment (Experimenter): Formalize `D(G) ≤ |G|` via prefix sums + pigeonhole,
  then instantiate `|⊕ ZMod mᵢ| = ∏ mᵢ`.
Analysis (Analyst): The pigeonhole step needs `card G < card (Fin (card G + 1))`,
  which holds unconditionally; the interval-sum split is the crux helper lemma.
Critique (Critic): The statement is non-vacuous (the conclusion produces a
  *nonempty* `t`), uses honest pigeonhole + telescoping (not `decide`/`rfl`),
  and is strictly different from EGZ (no fixed length).  Boundary: `card G ≥ 1`
  always holds since a group contains `0`.
Synthesis (PI): Combined into `davenport_zero_sum` and the product-form corollary
  `effective_threshold_prod`.
-- !-- end Lab Notes -- !--
-/

namespace Catalog.Applications.ErdosThreshold

open Finset

/-
**Prefix-sum telescoping.**  For a sequence `a : Fin N → G` over an additive
commutative group and `x ≤ y`, the difference of the two prefix sums (over the
indices `< y` and `< x`) equals the sum over the half-open interval `[x, y)`.
-/
theorem prefix_sum_split {N : ℕ} {G : Type*} [AddCommGroup G] (a : Fin N → G)
    (x y : ℕ) (hxy : x ≤ y) :
    (∑ i ∈ univ.filter (fun i : Fin N => (i : ℕ) < y), a i)
      - (∑ i ∈ univ.filter (fun i : Fin N => (i : ℕ) < x), a i)
      = ∑ i ∈ univ.filter (fun i : Fin N => x ≤ (i : ℕ) ∧ (i : ℕ) < y), a i := by
  rw [ sub_eq_iff_eq_add, ← Finset.sum_union ];
  · rcongr i;
    grind;
  · exact Finset.disjoint_left.mpr fun i hi₁ hi₂ => by linarith [ Finset.mem_filter.mp hi₁, Finset.mem_filter.mp hi₂ ] ;

/-
**Davenport constant upper bound `D(G) ≤ |G|`.**
Every sequence of `|G|` elements of a finite additive commutative group `G`
contains a nonempty subset (indeed a consecutive block) whose sum is `0`.
-/
theorem davenport_zero_sum {G : Type*} [AddCommGroup G] [Fintype G]
    (a : Fin (Fintype.card G) → G) :
    ∃ t : Finset (Fin (Fintype.card G)), t.Nonempty ∧ ∑ i ∈ t, a i = 0 := by
  by_contra! h_contra;
  -- By the pigeonhole principle, since there are $|G| + 1$ prefix sums and only $|G|$ possible values, at least two of these prefix sums must be equal.
  have h_pigeonhole : ∃ i j : Fin (Fintype.card G + 1), i < j ∧ (∑ k ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun v => v.val < i.val), a k) = (∑ k ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun v => v.val < j.val), a k) := by
    by_contra h_contra;
    exact absurd ( Fintype.card_le_of_injective ( fun i : Fin ( Fintype.card G + 1 ) => ∑ k with k.val < i.val, a k ) fun i j hij => le_antisymm ( not_lt.1 fun hi => h_contra ⟨ j, i, hi, hij.symm ⟩ ) ( not_lt.1 fun hj => h_contra ⟨ i, j, hj, hij ⟩ ) ) ( by simp +decide );
  obtain ⟨ i, j, hij, h ⟩ := h_pigeonhole;
  have h_zero_sum : ∑ k ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun v => v.val < j.val) \ Finset.univ.filter (fun v => v.val < i.val), a k = 0 := by
    rw [ ← Finset.sum_sdiff ( show Finset.filter ( fun v : Fin ( Fintype.card G ) => ( v : ℕ ) < i ) Finset.univ ⊆ Finset.filter ( fun v : Fin ( Fintype.card G ) => ( v : ℕ ) < j ) Finset.univ from fun x hx => Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨ Finset.mem_filter.mp hx |>.1, lt_trans ( Finset.mem_filter.mp hx |>.2 ) hij ⟩ ) ] at * ; aesop;
  exact h_contra _ ⟨ ⟨ i, by linarith [ Fin.is_lt i, Fin.is_lt j, show ( i : ℕ ) < j from hij ] ⟩, by aesop ⟩ h_zero_sum

end Catalog.Applications.ErdosThreshold

namespace Catalog.Applications.ErdosThreshold

open Finset

/-
The order of the product group `⊕ᵢ ZMod mᵢ` is the explicit product `∏ᵢ mᵢ`.
-/
theorem card_pi_zmod {k : ℕ} (m : Fin k → ℕ) [∀ i, NeZero (m i)] :
    Fintype.card (∀ i, ZMod (m i)) = ∏ i, m i := by
  simp +decide [ ZMod.card ]

/-
**Effective product-form threshold.**  Every sequence of `∏ᵢ mᵢ` elements of
`⊕ᵢ ZMod mᵢ` has a nonempty zero-sum subsequence.  The threshold `∏ᵢ mᵢ` is an
explicit, effectively computable instance of `C·(∏ᵢ mᵢ)^poly` (`C = poly = 1`).
-/
theorem effective_threshold_prod {k : ℕ} (m : Fin k → ℕ) [∀ i, NeZero (m i)]
    (a : Fin (∏ i, m i) → (∀ i, ZMod (m i))) :
    ∃ t : Finset (Fin (∏ i, m i)), t.Nonempty ∧ ∑ i ∈ t, a i = 0 := by
  obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ : ∃ t : Finset (Fin (Fintype.card (∀ i, ZMod (m i)))), t.Nonempty ∧ (∑ i ∈ t, (fun i => a (finCongr (by rw [card_pi_zmod]) i)) i) = 0 := by
    convert davenport_zero_sum _;
  refine' ⟨ Finset.image ( fun i => finCongr ( by rw [ card_pi_zmod ] ) i ) t, _, _ ⟩ <;> simp_all +decide [ Finset.sum_image ]

/-
**Multi-modulus Erdős–Ginzburg–Ziv (explicit threshold).**
Among any `2·(∏ᵢ mᵢ) - 1` integers there are exactly `∏ᵢ mᵢ` of them whose sum is
divisible *simultaneously* by every modulus `mᵢ`.  Derived from the catalog
theorem `Int.erdos_ginzburg_ziv`; the threshold `2·(∏ᵢ mᵢ) - 1` is explicit.
-/
theorem egz_multimodulus {k : ℕ} (m : Fin k → ℕ) {ι : Type*} {s : Finset ι}
    (a : ι → ℤ) (hs : 2 * (∏ i, m i) - 1 ≤ s.card) :
    ∃ t ⊆ s, t.card = ∏ i, m i ∧ ∀ i, (m i : ℤ) ∣ ∑ j ∈ t, a j := by
  obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ : ∃ t : Finset ι, t ⊆ s ∧ t.card = ∏ i, m i ∧ (↑(∏ i, m i) : ℤ) ∣ ∑ j ∈ t, a j := by
    convert Int.erdos_ginzburg_ziv ( fun i => a i ) _ using 1;
    exact hs;
  exact ⟨ t, ht.1, ht.2.1, fun i => dvd_trans ( mod_cast Finset.dvd_prod_of_mem _ ( Finset.mem_univ _ ) ) ht.2.2 ⟩

end Catalog.Applications.ErdosThreshold

This note collects small-case evidence for the two effective thresholds proved in
`EffectiveThreshold.lean` and `ProductForm.lean`.

## 1. Davenport threshold `D(G) ≤ |G|` (nonempty zero-sum subsequence)

Claim verified: every sequence of `|G|` elements of a finite abelian group `G`
has a nonempty zero-sum subsequence (`davenport_zero_sum`). The threshold equals
`|G|`, and for `G = ⊕ᵢ ZMod mᵢ` this is `∏ᵢ mᵢ` (`card_pi_zmod`).

Small cases of `|⊕ᵢ ZMod mᵢ| = ∏ᵢ mᵢ`:

| moduli (m₁,…,mₖ) | group                | threshold ∏mᵢ |
|------------------|----------------------|---------------|
| (2)              | ℤ/2                  | 2             |
| (3)              | ℤ/3                  | 3             |
| (2,2)            | ℤ/2 ⊕ ℤ/2            | 4             |
| (2,3)            | ℤ/2 ⊕ ℤ/3 ≅ ℤ/6      | 6             |
| (2,2,2)          | (ℤ/2)³               | 8             |

Sharpness check (the bound `|G|` is the right order of magnitude): in the cyclic
group `ℤ/n`, the constant sequence `(1,1,…,1)` of length `n-1` has **no** nonempty
zero-sum subsequence (any nonempty sub-sum is `j` with `1 ≤ j ≤ n-1`, never `0`).
So length `n-1` is not enough; the threshold `n = |ℤ/n|` is optimal for cyclic
groups. This confirms `D(ℤ/n) = n`, i.e. the bound is tight, not loose.

## 2. EGZ multi-modulus threshold `2·(∏mᵢ) − 1`

Claim verified: among `2·(∏ᵢmᵢ) − 1` integers, some `∏ᵢmᵢ` of them have a sum
divisible by every `mᵢ` simultaneously (`egz_multimodulus`, built on the catalog
theorem `Int.erdos_ginzburg_ziv`).

* `depthDist n`   — the depth distribution: for each value `t`, the number of

import Mathlib

namespace StackSortingDepth

/-! ## West's stack-sorting map -/

/-- `popLess x stack` pops off the top of `stack` (whose head is the top) every
element that is strictly smaller than `x`, returning the popped elements (in pop
order) together with the remaining stack. -/
def popLess (x : ℕ) : List ℕ → List ℕ × List ℕ
  | [] => ([], [])
  | (t :: ts) =>
      if t < x then
        (fun p => (t :: p.1, p.2)) (popLess x ts)
      else
        ([], t :: ts)

/-- One left-to-right pass of West's stack-sorting algorithm.  `sortPass xs
stack` processes the remaining input `xs` against the current `stack`: for each
new symbol it first flushes every smaller stack element to the output, then
pushes the symbol; when the input is exhausted the whole stack is flushed. -/
def sortPass : List ℕ → List ℕ → List ℕ
  | [], stack => stack
  | (x :: xs), stack =>
      let p := popLess x stack
      p.1 ++ sortPass xs (x :: p.2)

/-- West's stack-sorting map: one full pass starting from an empty stack. -/
def stackSort (l : List ℕ) : List ℕ := sortPass l []

/-! ## Permutation and length invariants -/

/-- `popLess` rearranges the stack: the popped elements together with the
remaining stack form a permutation of the original stack. -/
lemma popLess_perm (x : ℕ) (s : List ℕ) :
    ((popLess x s).1 ++ (popLess x s).2).Perm s := by
  induction' s with hd tl ih;
  · rfl;
  · by_cases h : hd < x <;> simp_all +decide [ popLess ];
    grind

/-- A full pass is a permutation of the input concatenated with the stack. -/
lemma sortPass_perm (xs stack : List ℕ) :
    (sortPass xs stack).Perm (xs ++ stack) := by
  induction' xs with x xs ih generalizing stack;
  · aesop;
  · convert List.Perm.trans ( List.Perm.append ( List.Perm.refl _ ) ( ih _ ) ) _ using 1;
    have h_perm : ((popLess x stack).1 ++ (popLess x stack).2).Perm stack :=
      popLess_perm x stack
    grind

/-- `stackSort l` is a permutation of `l`. -/
lemma stackSort_perm (l : List ℕ) : (stackSort l).Perm l := by
  simpa using sortPass_perm l []

> A uniformly random permutation of `[n]` has `depth(w) = Θ(n)` with high probability;

toward C4.
